f.title: MAHs selling drugs are responsible for post-market PV and GVP; selling under a name you control makes you a manufacturer
f.statement: Manufacturers or market authorization holders (MAHs) who sell drugs are responsible for post-market pharmacovigilance activities and good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP). Selling a drug under a name you control means you meet the definition of a manufacturer.
f.applicability: Persons involved in post-market PV for human pharmaceutical drugs (prescription and non-prescription), Schedule D biologics, Schedule C radiopharmaceuticals and medical gases

rows.quote: This guide is for manufacturers or market authorization holders (MAH), who sell drugs and are responsible for post-market pharmacovigilance activities and good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP). When you sell a drug under a name you control, you meet the definition of a manufacturer.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Mandatory kept ('are responsible for'), consistent with the POL-0041 row. Same boilerplate as HC-POL0041-2026-0003 in cat-ca-hc-pol-0041-2026-version; kept because each document version is curated on its own (no cross-document merge). Double-check: confirmed against the quote; classification kept. Below 90: 'are responsible for' is a statement of responsibility plus a definition rather than a shall/must, so Mandatory is a judgement call in a guidance document that only restates duties set by the regulations.

f.title: Implement GVP for the drugs you sell; Health Canada inspects compliance with the listed post-market PV regulations
f.statement: It is important to implement GVP to monitor and assess the safety and effectiveness of the drug(s) you sell, so that pharmacovigilance activities are conducted in a consistent, reliable and verifiable manner. Health Canada performs GVP inspections to assess compliance with the post-market pharmacovigilance and GVP requirements in the Food and Drug Regulations sections C.01.014.21, C.01.016 to C.01.020, C.01.050, C.08.007(1)(h), C.08.008(c) and C.08.003.
f.applicability: Persons involved in post-market PV for human pharmaceutical drugs (prescription and non-prescription), Schedule D biologics, Schedule C radiopharmaceuticals and medical gases

rows.quote: Health Canada performs GVP inspections to assess your compliance with the following post-market pharmacovigilance and GVP requirements outlined in the Food and Drug Regulations (regulations). C.01.014.21 C.01.016 to C.01.020 C.01.050 C.08.007(1)(h) C.08.008(c) C.08.003 It is important to implement GVP to monitor and assess the safety and effectiveness of the drug(s) you sell. GVP provides confidence that you have conducted pharmacovigilance activities in a consistent, reliable, and verifiable manner.
rows.review_note: Review: added - the GVP implementation expectation ('It is important to implement GVP', so Recommended) and the list of regulations Health Canada inspects against, which sets the inspection scope; not covered in POL-0041's extract under this wording. Double-check: confirmed against the quote; legal_basis matches the listed sections. Below 90: 'It is important to implement GVP' is not a should/must, so Recommended is a judgement call; the inspection sentence describes what Health Canada does and the regulations list is a bullet list flattened into the quote.

f.title: Ensure compliance with vigilance requirements applicable to products outside this guide's scope
f.statement: Although some product lines are out of scope of this guide, vigilance requirements may still apply to them; as the manufacturer or MAH, it is your responsibility to ensure compliance with the requirements of the Food and Drugs Act and regulations applicable to your products.
f.applicability: Product lines out of scope of GUI-0102: sperm and ova, medical devices, veterinary products, natural health products, cells, tissues and organs, whole blood and blood components, biocides (surface disinfectants and sanitizers)

f.title: Support alternate approaches to GVP guidance with adequate justification
f.statement: Guidance documents are administrative, not legal, instruments, so flexibility can be applied; however, to be acceptable, alternate approaches to the principles and practices in this document must be supported by adequate justification.
f.clause: Overview > Note about guidance documents in general
f.applicability: Persons involved in post-market PV for human pharmaceutical drugs (prescription and non-prescription), Schedule D biologics, Schedule C radiopharmaceuticals and medical gases

f.title: Discuss alternate approaches in advance with the relevant program area
f.statement: Alternate approaches should be discussed in advance with the relevant program area to avoid the possible finding that applicable statutory or regulatory requirements have not been met.
f.clause: Overview > Note about guidance documents in general
f.applicability: Persons involved in post-market PV for human pharmaceutical drugs (prescription and non-prescription), Schedule D biologics, Schedule C radiopharmaceuticals and medical gases
